# MOD fixtures

Every `.mod` file in this directory is generated by `gen_test_mod.py` (Python 3, standard
library only, fully deterministic). They contain **no third-party data**: both samples are
synthesised square/saw waves written by the script.

| file | how to regenerate | what it is |
|------|-------------------|------------|
| `test.mod` | `python3 -I tests/fixtures/gen_test_mod.py tests/fixtures/test.mod` | good file: 4 channels, 3 patterns, 2 samples (sample 1 looped, sample 2 not), uses `F03`, `F96`, `C20`, `C41`, `D15`, `B00`, period 428 on channel 0 at order 0 row 0 |
| `bad_len0.mod` | `python3 -I tests/fixtures/gen_test_mod.py --bad len0 ...` | song length 0 — must be rejected |
| `bad_len129.mod` | `... --bad len129 ...` | song length 129 — must be rejected |
| `bad_trunc_pattern.mod` | `... --bad trunc_pattern ...` | order table needs 3 patterns, file carries 1 — must be rejected |
| `bad_trunc_sample.mod` | `... --bad trunc_sample ...` | sample header claims more bytes than the file holds — must be rejected |

Dispatch script 9 regenerates all five into its scratch directory and `cmp`s them against
these files, so the committed bytes and the generator must stay in step. Change the
generator and the fixtures together, never one without the other.

`t-modplay` loads `test.mod` from the path given on its command line and expects the four
`bad_*.mod` files in the same directory (script 9 runs it as
`build/tests/t-modplay tests/fixtures/test.mod`).
